description: Renovate is scoped to the vertical-pod-autoscaler project only; the rest of the repository is handled by Dependabot. It keeps the Go base image in the VPA Dockerfiles on the latest patch release on all maintained branches, updates Go modules on master, and applies patch-level Go module updates on release branches.

packageRules.description: Dockerfiles: disable everything by default; the rule below opts specific updates back in.
Dockerfiles: keep the golang base image on the latest patch release of the Go minor already used by each branch. Minor/major Go bumps are done manually.
Go modules: only propose versions whose go.mod `go` directive is satisfied by ours, so dependency bumps never force a Go minor bump.
Go modules: also update indirect dependencies (Dependabot dependency-type: all). Rules that disable indirect updates must come after this one.
Go modules: indirect dependencies cannot be moved to a new major (module path) by us; the importing dependency has to do that.
Go modules: k8s.io/client-go only has legacy vN tags above v0.x (v11.0.0+incompatible); never propose them.

Go modules: k8s.io/kube-openapi and friends are untagged and must track the k8s.io/apimachinery release (their default branch may require a newer Go or a new structured-merge-diff major); don't bump their digests independently.
Go modules: pre-modules +incompatible pseudo-versions cannot follow newer commits once upstream adds a go.mod with a /vN module path; the importing dependency has to make that move.
Go modules: keep fsnotify at or below 1.9.0 to match the gomodguard restriction in vertical-pod-autoscaler/.golangci.yaml.
Go modules on master: bundle Kubernetes modules into one PR.
Go modules on master: bundle all other modules into one PR.
Go modules on release branches: start from nothing enabled; the rules below opt patch-level updates back in. Must come after the general gomod rules above (notably the indirect enable).
Go modules on release branches: Renovate normally offers only the highest non-major version; splitting patch from minor makes it offer the highest patch when the minor is blocked.
Go modules on release branches: allow patch updates.

Go modules on release branches: for pre-1.0 modules a minor bump is the patch-level release (e.g. golang.org/x/*), so allow those too. Kubernetes modules are v0.x but their minor is a Kubernetes minor, so they stay patch-only.

Go modules on release branches: k8s.io/kubernetes requires its staging modules at v0.0.0 via replace directives, so Go cannot keep them in lockstep, and its tag appears before the staging modules are published. Bump it manually together with k8s.io/api, apimachinery, client-go, etc.
Go modules on release branches: github.com/euank/go-kmsg-parser's v2.0.1 tag ships a go.mod without the /v2 module path, so Go rejects it; stay on v2.0.0+incompatible.
Go modules on release branches: everything that is still enabled goes into a single PR.
